ing: whole fish such as snapper or jack
st: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Rub the whole breadfruit skin with a little oil and put it on a baking tray.
Roast the breadfruit for [[75 minutes]], turning once, until the skin is charred and a knife slides into the center.
Rub the fish with the juice of [[2 limes]], [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper and the minced garlic. Let sit for [[20 minutes]].
Strip the thyme leaves and rub them on the fish, then dredge the fish in [[0.5 cup]] flour, shaking off extra.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 5 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through, then drain on paper towels.
Pour out all but 1 tablespoon oil and cook the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Peel and core the breadfruit, cut it into thick wedges, and serve alongside the fish topped with the onion.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the okra and [[3 cups]] broth and bring to a boil.
Add the callaloo or spinach, cover and simmer for [[20 minutes]] until very tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Simmer gently for [[10 minutes]] without boiling hard.
Remove the thyme stems. For a smooth soup, blend with a stick blender, or leave as is.
Taste, adjust salt and serve hot.
Soak the salt cod in cold water for [[8 hours]] or overnight, changing the water 3 times.
Drain, then cover with fresh water in a pot and boil for 10 minutes to remove more salt.
Drain, cool, and flake the fish with your fingers, removing any bones or skin.
Squeeze the flaked cod dry in a towel.
Mix the cod with the tomatoes, onion, bell pepper and chili.
Add [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, juice of 1 lime and [[0.25 tsp]] black pepper and toss.
Taste, and add pepper if needed. No salt is needed.
Serve at room temperature with bread or boiled root vegetables.

ing: or foil, cut in 10 inch squares
st: Peel and grate the sweet potatoes finely into a large bowl.
Stir in [[1 cup]] coconut, [[0.5 cup]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until thick.
If using banana leaves, soften them by passing over a flame or dipping in hot water.
Spoon about [[0.33 cup]] of batter in the center of each leaf piece.
Fold the leaf over the batter to make a flat parcel and tie with kitchen string, or wrap in foil.
Bring a pot with 2 inches of water to a boil and set a steamer rack or basket inside.
Steam the parcels covered for [[60 minutes]], adding water as needed.
Cool for 10 minutes, then unwrap and serve with saltfish or on its own.
Soak the salt cod in cold water for [[8 hours]] or overnight, changing the water a few times.
Boil the cod in fresh water for 10 minutes, then drain and flake it finely.
Mix [[1 cup]] flour with [[1 tsp]] baking powder in a bowl.
Stir in the flaked cod, onion, chili, [[1 tsp]] thyme and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Add [[0.5 cup]] water a little at a time to make a thick, scoopable batter.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Drop tablespoons of batter into the oil and fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Season the chicken with [[1.5 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper and the garlic.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat and add [[3 tbsp]] brown sugar.
Cook until the sugar bubbles and turns deep brown, about 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and brown on all sides in the caramel, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and thyme and cook 3 minutes.
Add the rice and pigeon peas and stir to coat.
Pour in the coconut milk and [[1.5 cups]] broth, then bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low for [[30 minutes]] until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve.
